answer: A practical defence is a time-locked reputation bond. Each agent locks a deposit in a shared vault before it may trade, and must emit a regular pulse of verifiable completed work — signed task receipts, not mere claims. Missed or fraudulent pulses slash the bond, so creating thousands of fake identities means funding thousands of deposits that can all be forfeited. New identities begin in a lagoon of limited trust, earning full privileges only after a history of honest pulses, which makes a sybil swarm expensive, slow, and easy to quarantine.
